Prove the two sides of the conjunction independently, and prove both propositions inside the `Iff` outright.

For the first conjunct, rewrite
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z',z)=\|z'-z\|.
\]
The map \(z'\mapsto z'-z\) is affine, and the norm is convex by the triangle inequality and positive homogeneity. Restricting this globally convex function to the convex set \(s\) gives the required `ConvexOn`.

For the left side of the `Iff`, represent \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(s)\) and \(y\in\operatorname{conv}(t)\) as finite convex combinations:
\[
x=\sum_i a_i x_i,\qquad y=\sum_j b_j y_j.
\]
Using the product coefficients \(a_i b_j\),
\[
x-y=\sum_{i,j}a_i b_j(x_i-y_j).
\]
The triangle inequality bounds \(\|x-y\|\) by the weighted average of the finitely many \(\|x_i-y_j\|\). Since the weights are nonnegative and sum to one, some pair \((i,j)\) has
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,y)\le \operatorname{dist}(x_i,y_j),
\]
with \(x_i\in s\) and \(y_j\in t\). Membership in the convex hull supplies the necessary nonempty finite representations.

For the right side, use set extensionality and characterize membership pointwise. Membership in the preimage says
\[
\forall i,\; \operatorname{elim}'(u)(i)\in t(i),
\]
while membership in `Set.tprod l t` recursively says that every component stored in the dependent list-product belongs to its corresponding set. Prove their equivalence by induction on `l`; `Nodup l` removes duplicate-coordinate ambiguity, and the hypothesis that every \(i\) occurs in `l` makes `List.TProd.elim'` total over all indices.

Having established both universal propositions independently, assemble the `Iff` by ignoring its premise in either direction.
